audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 4 and 6 disagreed with both the packet chart and their own whys: row 1 read Swain while whys[1] says 'Level 2 stays even', row 4 read Skill while whys[4] says his R swings the fight to him, row 6 read Swain while whys[6] says 'Late game evens'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Skill, Skill, Swain, Skill, Swain, Swain, Skill]; the mirror audit records exactly 'Row 1 to Skill, row 4 to Swain (7/10), row 6 to Skill'.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group, with row 4's rating set to 3/10 to invert the mirror's 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swain's spikes were unnumbered, and Demonic Ascension was described as if it had a fixed duration you could wait out.
audit.why: Kit: Death's Hand (Q) 7/6/5/4/3s at 750 range, Vision of Empire (W) 22/21/20/19/18s, Nevermove (E) 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 850 range, Demonic Ascension (R) 120s flat — 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.'
audit.corrected: 120s on his R plus the fact that it persists while he is draining a champion, so the counterplay is to leave rather than to outlast; Nevermove at 12s and Vision of Empire at 22s written into the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page consistently calls the root 'Nevermove (W)' — it is E. W is Vision of Empire, a long-range slow that also REVEALS you and feeds him a Soul Fragment. Six strings carried the wrong slot ('dodge the W seed', 'without W he can't lock you', 'Root you with W'). Also missing: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the outgoing one, so one sidestep is not enough, and his passive was described as a 'pull' when it is a heal off Soul Fragments.
audit.why: Riot text — E: 'launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' W: 'opens a demon eye that deals damage and slows enemies. Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment.' P: 'ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health.'
audit.corrected: Slot corrected everywhere it appeared, the return-pass root written in as the actual dodging instruction, and the passive described as a heal.

edits.before: W clone bails out any misstep and baits his answer. Only take the trade when Swain's Demonic Ascension is down.
edits.after: Even at 2: Nevermove is his root and it is E, 12s at rank 1 — until it lands he has only Death's Hand poke.

edits.before: Cyclone’s double knockup wins every committed brawl. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension is 120s and lasts while he drains you — burst him or leave; a long brawl only feeds the heal.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Burst when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, 850 range — it roots on the RETURN, so the danger is behind you. - Vision of Empire: 22s, and it reveals you. - Demonic Ascension: 120s, and it lasts while he drains.

edits.before: His drain. Burst when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It lasts as long as he drains a champion — leave, don't out-brawl.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return trip, not on the way out — dodge twice.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Burst when it’s down. When it is down — E-Q + R him.
edits.after: Nevermove (E) roots on the return, so sidestep twice; then E-Q and R before his drain ticks.

edits.before: Swain's level-3 root combo — Nevermove (W) into Death's Hand (Q) — punishes you hard if you E-Nimbus straight at him; his root pins you in the Q cone for heavy poke. Dodge the W seed, then E on a minion angle so you don't eat the root.
edits.after: Swain's level-3 root combo — Nevermove (E) into Death's Hand (Q) — punishes you hard if you E-Nimbus straight at him; the root pins you in the bolts for heavy poke. Nevermove roots on its return, so sidestep it twice, not once.

edits.before: Level 2 stays even; without W he can't lock you into his poke cone.
edits.after: Level 2 stays even; without Nevermove (E) he cannot lock you down.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 flatten as you dodge the W seed and E on safe angles.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 flatten as you sidestep Nevermove and E on safe angles.

edits.before: Dodge Nevermove (W) so his Q poke misses
edits.after: Sidestep Nevermove (E) going out and back

edits.before: Root you with W into the Death's Hand (Q) cone
edits.after: Root you with Nevermove into the Death's Hand

edits.before: Swain edges ahead from 3 on: his W root into Q poke chunks you, and his level-6 R heal turns your all-ins into free sustain unless you can burst him fast.
edits.after: Swain edges ahead from 3 on: his Nevermove root into Q poke chunks you, and his level-6 R heal turns your all-ins into free sustain unless you burst him fast.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even — Swain's short-range Q and no root yet mean you farm safely behind decoy. Respect his passive pull on low-HP minions.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even — Swain's short-range Q and no root yet mean you farm safely behind decoy. His passive heals him off soul fragments.

notes: Death's Hand is described by Riot as bolts that pierce, with more damage the more bolts hit you — the page calls it a 'cone', which is close enough in shape that I only changed it where the slot error forced a rewrite. Vision of Empire revealing you is now stated: it matters because Warrior Trickster's invisibility does not beat a reveal. Wukong's kit was null in the brief again, so no Wukong cooldowns were added.
